r: Although PP 1017 (a state of national emergency) was lifted while the case was pending, the Court decided it: courts decide moot cases when (1) there is a grave violation of the Constitution; (2) the situation is exceptional and paramount public interest is involved; (3) the issue requires controlling principles to guide the bench, the bar and the public; or (4) the case is capable of repetition yet evading review.
f: President Arroyo declared a state of national emergency (PP 1017, February 2006) and issued General Order No. 5; she lifted it a week later.
h: PP 1017 valid as a call to the armed forces to prevent lawless violence, but the President cannot issue decrees or take over private businesses without legislation; the warrantless arrests, the raid on the Daily Tribune and the dispersals were illegal.
x: Cite it for the four exceptions to mootness.
s: Four exceptions to mootness; PP 1017 upheld only as a calling-out.

r: Petitions against the Philippines’ withdrawal from the Rome Statute were dismissed: the withdrawal had already taken effect after the ICC received the notice, and senator-petitioners lacked standing because the Senate itself had not acted to assert a prerogative. The Court said the President’s power to withdraw from treaties is not unlimited, but did not void this withdrawal.
x: Use with Gatmaytan’s critique when a case turns on legislator standing or mootness.
g: Gatmaytan (‘Variant Technicalities’): the Court invented new technicalities, tying a legislator’s standing to an institutional act of the Senate and treating the completed withdrawal as a supervening event; the mootness exceptions could have applied.
s: ICC withdrawal: moot; senators lacked standing absent a Senate act.

n: City Government of Quezon City v. Ericta
r: An ordinance requiring private cemeteries to set aside 6% of their land for paupers’ graves is not a police measure but a taking of property without just compensation, and is void.
s: Cemetery set-aside for paupers: a taking without compensation.

r: Compelling newspapers to give COMELEC free print space is a taking of private property for public use that requires just compensation; COMELEC may buy the space, not commandeer it.
s: Free ‘COMELEC space’ in newspapers: a taking; must be paid for.

r: Requiring broadcasters to give COMELEC free airtime is valid: the airwaves are public property, a franchise is a privilege subject to amendment for the common good, and the requirement is a condition of the franchise, not a taking.
s: Free airtime from broadcasters: a valid franchise condition, not a taking.

n: Manila Memorial Park v. Secretary of Social Welfare and Development
r: The 20% senior citizens’ discount, which establishments may treat only as a tax deduction rather than a full tax credit, is a valid exercise of police power, not a taking requiring full compensation.
s: Senior citizens’ discount as a tax deduction: police power.

r: Minors, suing for themselves and for generations yet unborn, may sue to protect the right to a balanced and healthful ecology (Art. II, Sec. 16), which the Court treated as self-executing and judicially enforceable; timber license agreements are not contracts protected by the non-impairment clause.
g: Gatmaytan (‘The Illusion of Intergenerational Equity’): the standing of future generations was obiter, not needed to decide whether the petitioners had a cause of action.
s: Intergenerational standing; Art. II, Sec. 16 enforceable.

r: RA 10153, synchronizing ARMM elections with national elections and letting the President appoint officers-in-charge, was upheld. Constitutional provisions are read together; one mandate is not given priority over another unless the Constitution makes its primacy clear. The factual basis of a presidential certification of urgency is generally not reviewed.
s: ARMM synchronization upheld; harmonize provisions; urgency certification.

r: Where the words of a law are clear, plain and free from ambiguity, they are given their literal meaning and applied without interpretation; interpretation is resorted to only where a literal reading would be impossible, absurd or unjust.
s: Verba legis: clear words are applied, not interpreted.

r: The US Supreme Court established judicial review: it is the province of the judiciary to say what the law is, and a law repugnant to the Constitution is void. The US Constitution does not expressly grant the power; ours does (Art. VIII, Secs. 1 and 5).
s: Origin of judicial review in the US.

r: The capital recovery levy under LOI 1465, collected for the benefit of a private company, was an invalid tax because it lacked a public purpose. The operative fact doctrine does not apply where it would let the beneficiary of the void law keep what it collected.
s: Operative fact refused: the beneficiary of a void levy must refund.

n: Social Justice Society v. Dangerous Drugs Board
r: Congress cannot add to the qualifications of senators fixed by Art. VI, Sec. 3: mandatory drug testing of candidates (RA 9165, Sec. 36(g)) was void as an added qualification. Random testing of students and employees was upheld; mandatory testing of persons charged with crimes was void.
s: Drug testing of candidates adds a qualification: void.

r: Giving Makati its own legislative district on conversion into a city was valid: a city with at least 250,000 inhabitants is entitled to at least one representative, and Congress may create a district by the law that converts the city. Challenges based on incumbents’ term limits were premature.
s: New city, new district: valid.

r: A detention prisoner, like a convict, remains under the court’s custody and cannot leave confinement to practise a profession; detention is not suspended because of the detainee’s occupation.
s: Detainees, like convicts, cannot practise their profession.

r: The Sandiganbayan may order the preventive suspension of a sitting senator charged under RA 3019. Suspension under Sec. 13 is mandatory once a valid information is filed and is a precaution, not a punishment, so it is distinct from the Senate’s power to discipline its Members under Art. VI, Sec. 16(3); it may not exceed 90 days.
s: Court-ordered preventive suspension of a senator: valid.

r: A tax classification is valid if it (1) rests on substantial distinctions, (2) is germane to the purpose of the law, (3) is not limited to existing conditions only, and (4) applies equally to all members of the same class. The simplified net income tax scheme for professionals was upheld.
s: The four-part test for a valid tax classification.

r: Once a party-list nominee has been proclaimed, taken the oath and assumed office, questions on the nominee’s qualifications belong to the HRET; questions on the party-list organization itself remain with COMELEC.
s: Seated party-list nominee: HRET; the group: COMELEC.

n: Ang Bagong Bayani-OFW Labor Party v. COMELEC
r: The party-list system was read as a social-justice tool for the marginalized and underrepresented: parties had to represent such sectors and their nominees had to belong to them. Abandoned by Atong Paglaum (2013).
s: Party-list only for the marginalized (later abandoned).

r: The 2% threshold for additional seats is void because it makes the 20% allocation impossible to fill. Seats are filled in rounds: one guaranteed seat for each group with 2%, additional seats in proportion to votes, then one each down the ranking; the three-seat cap is valid.
s: The party-list seat formula; no 2% floor for additional seats.

r: The RA 7227 proviso making the Olongapo City mayor the SBMA chairman violated Art. IX-B, Sec. 7: no elective official is eligible for appointment to another public office during his tenure, and resigning after the appointment does not cure it.
s: Elective official appointed to another office: void.

r: Labo lost Philippine citizenship by naturalization in Australia and so could not serve as mayor of Baguio; the candidate with the second-highest votes could not be proclaimed in his place.
s: Naturalized abroad: not qualified; no second placer.

r: COMELEC gravely abused its discretion in cancelling Poe’s certificate of candidacy for President. A foundling is presumed natural-born under the Constitution and international law, and her residence could be counted from her return in 2005.
s: Foundling presumed natural-born; COC cancellation reversed.
